assumptions: The bound v2 research remains relevant to the v4 candidate's underlying Polish construction-reuse market, while the new recurring-retainer and portfolio-gating mechanics have no direct validation in that research.

Field surveys, hazardous-material work, removal, transport, storage, testing, and regulated waste handling can be contractually delegated to qualified and insured specialists without the venture taking inventory or inadvertently assuming operator-of-record duties.

The founder can sustain the stated 15-20 hours per week within the founder profile's part-time limit during validation, but a separate operating team would be required for material project throughput.

The initial 75000 PLN capital envelope is adequate for an asset-light pilot only if customers fund specialist-heavy audits and pass-through work rather than the venture financing delivery or inventory.
Absent customer commitments, site-level yield data, or margin observations are treated as material uncertainty rather than proof of no demand or impossible economics.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid Polish portfolio pilots covering a meaningful forward pipeline, with retained renewal intent and site-level observations of screening time, gate accuracy, full-audit conversion, buyer reservations, completed sales, removal and logistics costs, contribution margin, CAC payback, and written legal and insurance acceptance of the exact operator-of-record contract flow.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Moving the decision point to a recurring portfolio review and gating full audits before procurement, deinstallation, or waste classification closes reuse options is a coherent response to the known cost problem. It could prevent uneconomic specialist work and create a useful paired dataset, but the ability to estimate net recoverable value from lightweight early-site data is still only a hypothesis, and an integrated audit-to-marketplace workflow is not novel given Concular.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Polish separation duties and deadline-sensitive demolition decisions create genuine coordination and compliance pain. However, pre-demolition audits are not generally mandated, authorised waste entities already offer an alternative compliance route, the economic benefit of audits is uncertain, and no reviewed evidence shows that owners or contractors will add a recurring screening retainer to their budgets.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: A retainer plus gated project fees is more resilient than relying on commissions, and keeping inventory and specialist costs outside the fee can protect cash conversion. Yet retainer price, screening cost, gate-pass rate, completed-sale volume, contribution margin, repeat rate, CAC, payback, and owner earnings are all unknown. JRC's roughly EUR 3000-5000 audit-cost evidence, uncertain project benefit, free or no-commission substitutes, and RAEDIFICARE's approximately EUR 714 reported average order value make the proposed fee stack and scalable founder-net-worth path fragile until demonstrated.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Recurring commercial-property and demolition portfolios with substantial sites and pre-sellable non-structural components form a much clearer beachhead than a general salvage marketplace. The segment may nonetheless be narrow after applying site size, early-data availability, product-status, removal-cost, buyer-density, and value-to-cost gates, and the research does not quantify the resulting Polish serviceable market or repeat project volume.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Early access to a few Polish portfolios and embedding the economic gate in their planning process could support a local specialist position. There is no established exclusive channel, right, standard, or supply relationship, while Concular already offers the close full-stack audit, inventory, marketplace, logistics, and assurance substitute and other marketplaces suppress transaction fees. A dominant position is therefore possible only after winning scarce portfolio access and execution data, not inherent in the current structure.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A proven portfolio-screening wedge could extend into more component classes, contractor accounts, regions, benchmarking, procurement support, and workflow software. Each adjacent move depends on buyer liquidity and introduces additional testing, conformity, waste-status, warranty, insurance, or logistics complexity, while a planned EU digital audit platform may absorb part of the data-layer opportunity.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Paired site features, gate decisions, buyer criteria, removal yields, timing, and completed outcomes could improve triage and quoting with accumulated volume; recurring workflow access may also create modest switching costs. Those assets do not exist yet, competitors can collect similar data, customer and project frequency may be too low for fast learning, and future public digital-audit infrastructure could commoditise inventory information.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Customers could gain one early go/no-go decision, less wasted audit spend, and delegated coordination without the venture owning inventory. The research does not establish accuracy, savings, speed, trust, or realised recoveries relative to a demolition contractor, licensed waste operator, consultant, or Concular, and a new retainer can be an added cost rather than a compelling advantage if few sites pass the gate.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Poland's 2025 construction-waste separation duties, EU circularity policy, and movement toward digital pre-demolition information create attention and workflow change now. The tailwind is qualified because audit guidance remains non-binding, direct reuse economics are uncertain, and a public European data platform could strengthen the category while weakening a private inventory-data advantage.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Targeting a small number of portfolio owners, demolition contractors, property managers, architects, and licensed operators is identifiable and more repeatable than acquiring one-off sellers. No paid access, channel commitment, sales-cycle evidence, or contractor incentive alignment is established, and obtaining early site records plus authority before procurement is a relationship-heavy enterprise sale that may be difficult to originate part-time.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The analytical screening layer fits the founder and a pilot can be asset-light within the stated time and capital constraints if specialists bear delivery roles. Execution still crosses lot-specific product-versus-waste status, BDO scope, title, hazardous materials, testing, insurance, removal damage, storage, transport, buyer reservations, and demolition deadlines; an operator-of-record agreement does not automatically remove the venture's own duties, and material throughput requires a full-time operating team.

highest_value_structural_change: Embed the screen as a white-label module inside one licensed demolition or waste operator's existing annual portfolio contracts, require a minimum committed site pipeline, and release a full audit only after buyer-backed indications or deposits establish recoverable demand; this would replace a separate retainer sale with an existing budget and channel while testing liquidity before specialist cost is incurred.
main_structural_strength: The portfolio-level control point creates the possibility of repeat paid access before irreversible demolition decisions and uses a value-to-delivery-cost gate to avoid deploying expensive specialists on plainly uneconomic sites.
primary_score_limiter: The redesign depends simultaneously on customers paying a recurring screening retainer and on sparse pre-audit site data predicting net recoverable value accurately enough to improve economics; neither dependency is supported by the bound evidence.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: JRC reports roughly EUR 3000-5000 audit costs for demolition projects up to EUR 300000 while finding economic effectiveness uncertain, especially for smaller projects; this directly challenges whether screening can surface enough surplus value to fund the audit-and-coordination layer consistently.
